build: dancer's frame — narrow shoulders, defined collarbone, small waist that flares to rounded hips
hair: dark brown locs, shoulder-length, often wrapped in silk or pinned high; the ends catch light with a warm undertone
complexion: deep warm brown with golden undertones; a small crescent scar on her left temple from childhood
face: heart-shaped with a wide, mobile mouth and eyes that telegraph every feeling — she cannot hide; her expressions move through her face like weather
signature_feature: her hands — long-fingered, expressive, constantly moving when she talks; he notices the way her fingers trace the rim of a glass, the deliberate care in how she touches fabric or a person's arm
second_celebrated_feature: the curve of her neck and collarbone when she turns her head — vulnerable, elegant, impossible to look away from
signature_habits: she hums while working — Yoruba folk melodies her grandmother taught her, unconscious and soothing; she keeps a small leather journal where she sketches design ideas in pen, never digital; she says 'Ẹ kú ìrìn' (safe travels) to people leaving, even casually; she touches her own sternum when she's nervous or thinking hard, a self-soothing gesture
occupation: textile designer and owner of a small sustainable fabric studio in Brooklyn — she sources organic cotton and natural dyes, works with artisans, creates limited-run collections; the space is her sanctuary and her financial lifeline

current_crisis.event: her studio's primary supplier just went bankrupt without warning; her spring collection — already promised to three boutiques and a small fashion house — cannot be produced; she has forty-eight hours to either find replacement sourcing or lose the contracts and face a cash-flow collapse that will shutter the business she built over four years
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic layered with a suffocating sense of powerlessness — she is watching something she loves die and cannot stop it
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find someone — anyone — with capital and connections in textiles who will take her seriously instead of patting her hand like she's a child with a craft hobby

wound.core: she believes that wanting something badly enough means she will eventually lose it — that her hunger for stability and creative autonomy is a curse that invites collapse
wound.surfacing_hint: when things start going well, she sabotages quietly or waits for the other shoe to drop; she over-apologizes; she flinches when praised; under pressure, she spirals into catastrophizing and becomes almost paralyzed by the certainty that she is about to fail
